name: Hypothyroid or Hypothyroidism

category.name: General Systemic
category.part: AME Physical Examination Information and Disposition Tables

what_to_bring: A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with the treating physician performed no more than 90 days before the AME exam. (Diagnosis of Central Hypothyroidism should be evaluated by an endocrinologist.) It must include a detailed summary of the history of the condition; current medications, dosage, and side effects (if any); physical exam findings; results of any testing performed; diagnosis; assessment; plan (prognosis); and follow-up.
Lab: Performed within 90 days of the AME exam to include:
Any other lab already performed (Ex. T3, Free T4) by the treating physician.
Imaging: Copies of any imaging reports (MRI, CT, ultrasound, X-ray) already performed.
Any other testing deemed clinically necessary by the treating physician.

rows.label: A

rows.label: B
rows.evaluation_data: See the CACI - Hypothyroidism Worksheet . This will require a current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with the treating physician no more than 90 days before the AME exam AND TSH. Note: As of 1/25/2023, TSH up to 9.9 can be considered for CACI if other criteria are met.

rows.evaluation_data: Submit the following for FAA review: - 1. A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with the treating physician performed no more than 90 days before the AME exam. (Diagnosis of Central Hypothyroidism should be evaluated by an endocrinologist.) It must include a detailed summary of the history of the condition; current medications, dosage, and side effects (if any); physical exam findings; results of any testing performed; diagnosis; assessment; plan (prognosis); and follow-up. - 2. Lab: Performed within 90 days of the AME exam to include: - Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH), and - Any other lab already performed (Ex. T3, Free T4) by the treating physician. - 3. Imaging: Copies of any imaging reports (MRI, CT, ultrasound, X-ray) already performed. - - Submit the interpretive report on paper and imaging on CD in DICOM readable format (there must be a file named 'DICOMDIR' in the root directory of the CD-ROM). Please verify the CD will display the images before sending. Retain a copy of all films as a safeguard if lost in the mail. - 4. Any other testing deemed clinically necessary by the treating physician.
rows.evaluation_data_html:
Submit the following for FAA review:

  • 1. A current, detailed Clinical Progress Note generated from a clinic visit with the treating physician performed no more than 90 days before the AME exam. (Diagnosis of Central Hypothyroidism should be evaluated by an endocrinologist.) It must include a detailed summary of the history of the condition; current medications, dosage, and side effects (if any); physical exam findings; results of any testing performed; diagnosis; assessment; plan (prognosis); and follow-up.

  • 2. Lab: Performed within 90 days of the AME exam to include:

    • Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH), and
    • Any other lab already performed (Ex. T3, Free T4) by the treating physician.
  • 3. Imaging: Copies of any imaging reports (MRI, CT, ultrasound, X-ray) already performed.
    • Submit the interpretive report on paper and imaging on CD in DICOM readable format (there must be a file named 'DICOMDIR' in the root directory of the CD-ROM). Please verify the CD will display the images before sending. Retain a copy of all films as a safeguard if lost in the mail.
  • 4. Any other testing deemed clinically necessary by the treating physician.
